title: How to Avoid Debate: Scalable AI Safety via Interactive Proofs
hook: AI safety via debate assumes two equally matched AIs arguing before a human judge. This paper shows a weak verifier can be convinced by a single powerful AI instead — no opponent required.
key_points: Debate-based verification needs two competing, comparably capable AI provers, one of which is truthful — an assumption that may not hold in practice.
The authors instead study single-prover interactive proofs: one powerful AI convincing a weak verifier (a human) that its output is correct, without a rival AI to check it.
Prior single-prover interactive-proof results break down when the computation calls an oracle, like human judgment or an external database — this paper extends them to that setting.

They give doubly-efficient single-prover proofs/arguments for oracle-aided ('relativizing') computations in two cases: robust computations tolerant of some wrong oracle answers, and computations where the oracle is a low-degree polynomial.
Upshot: interactive verification of powerful AI may be possible without needing a second, equally capable AI to debate against.
content_html: "AI safety via debate" pits two AI models against each other to convince a human judge which one is telling the truth — but that only works if the two AIs are comparably capable and at least one is honest. This paper asks what's possible without that setup.
extra_html: The authors initiate the study of single-prover interactive proofs for AI safety: can one powerful AI convince a weak verifier (a human) that its output is correct, without a second AI to check its work? Classic single-prover interactive-proof results don't carry over directly, because they don't handle computations that call an oracle mid-computation — like consulting human judgment or querying an external database — which is exactly the kind of computation real AI safety verification involves. The paper's contribution is doubly-efficient single-prover proofs and arguments for these oracle-aided ("relativizing") computations, covering two structured cases: computations that are robust (the output doesn't change even if a small fraction of oracle answers are wrong), and computations where the oracle behaves as a low-degree polynomial. Together, these results suggest interactive verification of powerful AI systems may be achievable under structured or noise-tolerant oracle access, without requiring debate's two-competing-prover setup. Liyan Chen, Yael Tauman Kalai, and Zoe Xi, arXiv 2026.

related.title: Model Evaluation for Extreme Risks
related.hook: General-purpose AI tends to pick up dangerous capabilities alongside useful ones. So test for those capabilities directly — before you ship, not after.

related.title: Frontier AI Regulation
related.hook: How do you regulate models too new to have rules yet? This paper sketches three building blocks: set standards, make labs report, then enforce.

flashcards.prompt: What assumption does AI safety via debate rely on that this paper tries to avoid?
flashcards.back_html: Debate assumes two AI provers of comparable ability compete against each other, and that one of them is truthful — an assumption that may not hold if capabilities are mismatched or both provers are unreliable.

flashcards.prompt: What is a 'single-prover interactive proof' as used in this paper?

choices.text: A setup where one powerful AI (the prover) convinces a weak verifier its output is correct, with no second AI needed
A proof requiring two AIs to agree before any output is trusted
A formal proof that debate always produces the correct answer

flashcards.explanation_html: Unlike debate, this approach only needs one prover and one weak (human) verifier — removing the need for a comparably capable, truthful second AI.

flashcards.prompt: Why don't prior single-prover interactive-proof results directly apply to AI safety verification?
flashcards.back_html: Those results don't handle computations that call an oracle mid-computation — such as human judgment or an external database — which is exactly the setting real AI safety verification needs.

flashcards.prompt: In which two oracle settings do the authors give doubly-efficient single-prover proofs?

choices.text: Robust computations tolerant of some incorrect oracle answers, and computations where the oracle is a low-degree polynomial
Only computations with zero access to any oracle
Only computations where the oracle is always perfectly reliable

flashcards.explanation_html: The two structured cases are: (1) robustness to a small fraction of wrong oracle answers, and (2) oracles that behave as low-degree polynomials — both allow efficient proofs despite the oracle dependency.
